literal.prompt: Какое средство повышения заметности пешеходного перехода помогает водителю увидеть пешехода благодаря положительному контрасту?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The question asks which crossing-visibility measure makes a pedestrian easier to identify using positive contrast. FHWA specifically assigns that function to crosswalk lighting at L42; the other options are the same FHWA enhancement family but use visible patterns or driver signs/markings at L33, L39, L45.

literalGroups.literal: Цель освещения перехода — обеспечить положительный контраст, чтобы водителю было легче заметить пешехода. Высоковидимая разметка, знаки и STOP/YIELD-разметка тоже относятся к мерам безопасности перехода, но используют другие сигналы.
literalGroups.primaryGround: FHWA states that crosswalk lighting should use positive contrast to make pedestrian identification easier. It treats high-visibility crosswalks and signing/pavement markings as other crossing enhancements with distinct functions.

literalGroups.literal: FHWA перечисляет парные полосы и рисунки «континенталь» и «лестница»: такие узоры видны водителям и пешеходам дальше, чем обычные поперечные линии.
literalGroups.primaryGround: FHWA names bar pairs, continental, and ladder patterns and says they are visible to both drivers and pedestrians from farther away than traditional transverse-line crosswalks.

literalGroups.literal: FHWA указывает, что в США на многополосной дороге агентства могут поставить такой знак за 20–50 футов до размеченного перехода, в зависимости от закона штата.
literalGroups.primaryGround: FHWA says agencies may use STOP Here for Pedestrians or YIELD Here to Pedestrians signs 20–50 feet before a marked crossing on multilane roads, depending on State law; the note preserves can/modality and jurisdiction.

literalGroups.literal: Полоса STOP или YIELD может дополнять знак и указывать водителю место остановки или уступки.
literalGroups.primaryGround: FHWA says a STOP or YIELD bar may be installed to supplement the sign and mark where drivers should stop or yield.

literalGroups.literal: FHWA рекомендует размещать светильники впереди пешехода по ходу движения, чтобы избежать силуэтного эффекта.
literalGroups.primaryGround: FHWA says forward placement of crosswalk luminaires helps avoid a silhouette effect; this additional own-option fact extends beyond the prompt and key.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.note: FHWA перечисляет парные полосы и рисунки «континенталь» и «лестница»: такие узоры видны водителям и пешеходам дальше, чем обычные поперечные линии.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: Each noun phrase is grammatically compatible with «Какое средство ... помогает ...?» as a crossing-visibility measure.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: High-visibility crosswalk markings are a plausible competing visibility feature. FHWA says their patterns can be seen from farther away; they do not provide the positive-contrast illumination named in the prompt. The note adds the three pattern examples and their visibility fact.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.note: FHWA указывает, что в США на многополосной дороге агентства могут поставить такой знак за 20–50 футов до размеченного перехода, в зависимости от закона штата.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: Each noun phrase is grammatically compatible with «Какое средство ... помогает ...?» as a crossing-visibility measure.

It is not illumination; the corrected note keeps the FHWA U.S. context, optional modality, state-law condition, and distance.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: STOP/YIELD pavement bars are another closely related road marking and may supplement signs. They indicate where drivers should stop or yield, rather than illuminate pedestrians; the note states this role.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: Each noun phrase is grammatically compatible with «Какое средство ... помогает ...?» as a crossing-visibility measure.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: Crosswalk lighting is the unique option that FHWA assigns the positive-contrast function for helping drivers identify pedestrians. Its note adds the forward-luminaire placement guidance and silhouette rationale.

entries.correctNoteNewFact: The correct note adds FHWA’s forward luminaire placement to avoid a pedestrian silhouette (L42); this fact is about the lighting option itself and goes beyond prompt/key.
entries.absoluteDifficulty: Easy: broad adult audiences readily recognize lighting as a way to make a pedestrian visible; each distractor is a plausible crossing-visibility enhancement from the same FHWA page, and distinguishing the positive-contrast function requires only the functional cue stated in the question.

cycle1DirectedFixes.D1: The prompt now asks for a crossing-visibility function. All four answers are FHWA crossing-visibility enhancements; each is plausible, while only lighting uses positive contrast to make a pedestrian easier to identify.
cycle1DirectedFixes.D2: The sign note now attributes the recommendation to FHWA, says agencies may use it on U.S. multilane roads, and retains the State-law qualification.
